content.text:
I have now read every paragraph in the document (p0000–p0074). Analysis:

- **§3.1 (p0019)** — the Company's only payment obligation is **30% of Net Sales in excess of $11,000 per calendar month** — a purely transactional, sales-based fee. No floor, no minimum spend, no fixed hosting fee (HDI bears all development/hosting costs under §§1.2, 1.6, 1.7).
- Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "volume", "quantity", "guarantee", "take or pay", "purchase" returned no responsive commitment language anywhere.
- **§4.2 (p0026–p0029)** is an early-termination payment keyed to *actual* Net Sales (and zero if Net Sales are ≤ $800,000) — it is a termination fee, not a shortfall/take-or-pay make-whole, and belongs to the termination-fee rule, not MINCOMMIT.
- **§6.1 (p0037)** is an exclusivity/non-compete restriction, not a volume cap on Customer usage.

The preferred position is met on its material terms, so no redline.

input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on the Company, so it sits at the preferred position. The Company's sole payment obligation (§3.1, p0019) is a pure revenue share — 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 in a calendar month — payable monthly on actual sales only (§3.2, p0020), with quarterly reconciliation for refunds and exchanges (§3.3). There is no committed spend, no minimum volume, no shortfall or make-whole mechanic, and no fixed hosting fee: HDI bears all design, development, hosting and promotion costs (§§1.2, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8). Full-text searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "volume", "quantity", "guarantee" and "take or pay" returned nothing responsive. Two clauses were examined and are not take-or-pay: (i) the §4.2 Termination Payment (p0026) is an early-termination fee calculated off actual trailing 12-month Net Sales, and is nil where those Net Sales do not exceed $800,000 — it does not require the Company to generate any level of sales and is properly assessed under the termination-fee rule rather than double-flagged here; and (ii) §6.1 exclusivity restricts competing Deerskin web projects but imposes no volume commitment or usage cap. Noted only for the record (not a deviation): the fee threshold in §3.1 operates in our favour as a floor below which nothing is owed.
